the combination of rapid heating rates, mechanical vibration and the chemistry of the intercalants in the clays are key factors in determining the dispersion and the resulting mechanical properties of the nanocomposites.

the processing of these nanocomposites requires a balance of the clay surfactant chemistry, heating rate and mechanical vibration to obtain the best mechanical properties.

a rapid heating rate, combined with the use of a primary ammonium surfacant, and a moderate level of mechanical vibration, can produce epoxy/clay nancomposites with a high degree of exfoliation and a significant improvement in flexural strength.

processing conditions and clay chemistry can have a significant influence on nanomorphology, which in turn can affect macroscale properties.
processing conditions and clay chemistry can significantly affect the structure–property relationships of epoxy/clay nanomposites.
